text:
elaine: fyi master is red on linux-matrix after today's lockfile regen. looks like a dependency with an optional extra broke a test matrix :/

mike: ugh, which package? any stack? :eyes:

elaine: seeing ImportError in pytests for `storage.s3` helpers — traceback points at `dependency_x[aws]` import. local env passes. CI installs via `pip install -r constraints.txt` from the regen artifacts.

jon: can you paste the failing traceback?

elaine: sure — paste below:
```
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dependency_x.aws'

venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/dependency_x/__init__.py:4: in <module>
    from .aws import S3Client
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dependency_x.aws'
```

elaine: interestingly, wheel for dependency_x on linux was built without the extra, so import fails at runtime. macos-green.

ci-bot: deploy-checker: job linux-matrix/pylint-3.10 failed (exit 1). Full logs: https://ci.internal/3832/logs

mike: my hunch: when lock regen happened we pinned dependency_x to a version that changed how extras are packaged (maybe moved optional modules to a separate package or requires extras to be installed explicitly). pip's resolver can produce a constraints.txt that doesn't include extras unless the root req asked for them.

sara: right — if our package declares `dependency_x[aws]` in extras for storage, but the constraints were generated from top-level entries and lost the extra, CI could install plain `dependency_x`. Did the regen script use `pip-compile --generate-hashes` or poetry export?

elaine: regen was running `poetry lock && poetry export --without-hashes -f requirements.txt`. I think poetry export drops extras unless `--with` flags used.

harry: quick triage: is the import in our code guarded by optional dependency? If not, we probably need to either pin dep_x[aws] explicitly in our pyproject or change the regen.

jon: I can run a quick local repro with a fresh venv and a requirements.txt generated the same way. if someone can upload the exact regen artifact I can pip install it here and try to reproduce.

elaine: artifact uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/constraints/3832104567/requirements.txt

mike: i'll run `pip install -r requirements.txt` in a linux container now. if it installs dependency_x without the extra, we can try editing the file to `dependency_x[aws]==X.Y.Z` and confirm tests pass.

(10m later)

mike: confirmed — requirements.txt has `dependency_x==2.1.0` (no extras). installing `dependency_x[aws]==2.1.0` makes the failing test import succeed locally.

ci-bot: note: edit made to regen job config at 3832104567 by github-actions-bot (comment) — job will be re-run if manual flag set.

sara: two actionable options: 1) change regen to preserve extras (preferred) 2) add explicit `dependency_x[aws]` to our pyproject/requirements to ensure constraints include extras. Which do we want short-term?

harry: short-term: add explicit `dependency_x[aws]` to pyproject under optional-deps or requirements-dev so the export includes it. long-term: fix regen script to map extras into exported requirements.

elaine: i'll open a tiny PR to pin the extra and trigger a quick CI rerun. tagging @jon for review — it's a one-line change in pyproject.

jon: pinged. will review asap. if CI still flakes after that we can trigger a bisect of the lock regen commit range.

mike: if we need a bisect, i can run a quick `git bisect run ./scripts/regenerate-constraints.sh` against the last two merges and reproduce which commit caused the change.

elaine: thanks — created PR 1247 with the explicit extra. will watch CI. :thumbsup:

jon: approved and merged. re-run queued.

(5m)

ci-bot: linux-matrix job re-run finished — all green.

elaine: confirming green in dashboard. closing the loop: regen pipeline will be updated this week to include extras mapping. i'll add a note to infra runbook and the regen README.

sara: great follow-up — thanks everyone for the quick turn. :tada:
